title: It's Not What the Image Shows: Irrelevant Context Destabilises VLM Judges Without Informing Them
abstract: arXiv:2609.37863v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly used in place of human annotators, making it important that substitutability tests reflect the model rather than incidental evaluation conditions. We introduce MIST, the Misleading-Image Stress Test: 200 English sentences, each built around a phrase readable either figuratively or literally and shown with an aligned image depicting its reading, a misleading image depicting the opposite, or no image at all. The guidelines require the label to be decided from the sentence alone, so no image should change any answer. We expected each image to pull a judge's labels toward the sense it depicts, and neither kind did. Across thirteen VLM judges, an aligned image changed 20.5% of labels and a misleading one 19.4%, close for every judge and both above the 11.6% produced by deleting the ignore-the-image instruction with the image left in place. Yet only 37% of the labels that differ between the two

translated_title: 重要的不是图像展示了什么：无关上下文在不提供信息的情况下动摇VLM评判器的稳定性
translated_abstract: 视觉语言模型（VLM）越来越多地被用来替代人类标注者，因此替代性测试的结果应当反映模型本身的能力，而非偶然的评估条件。我们提出了MIST（误导性图像压力测试）：包含200个英文句子，每个句子都围绕一个既可以按比喻义也可以按字面义解读的短语构建，并以三种条件之一呈现：一幅与句子含义一致的图像、一幅描绘相反含义的误导性图像，或者完全不配图像。标注指南要求标签仅依据句子本身来决定，因此任何图像都不应改变答案。我们原本预期每种图像都会将评判器的标签拉向其描绘的含义，但两种图像都没有产生这种预期效果。在十三个VLM评判器上，一致的图像改变了20.5%的标签，误导性图像改变了19.4%，对所有评判器而言两者数值接近，且都高于在保留图像的情况下仅删除“忽略图像”指令所产生的11.6%变化率。然而，在两种图像条件下标签不同的案例中，只有37%……（摘要至此截断）
tldr: 本文提出MIST误导性图像压力测试，揭示无关图像——无论与句义一致还是相反——都会以几乎相同的幅度（约20%）动摇VLM评判器的标签判断，且动摇幅度甚至超过删除“忽略图像”指令的影响，表明图像是作为干扰性上下文而非信息来源起作用，威胁了VLM替代人类标注者的可靠性。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces MIST, a misleading-image stress test revealing that irrelevant images—whether aligned or misleading—destabilise VLM judges' labels at nearly identical rates (~20%), even exceeding the effect of removing the ignore-the-image instruction, showing that images act as destabilising context rather than informative evidence and threatening the reliability of VLMs as human annotator substitutes.
